Problem and change

Ordinary CPU configuration changes and controller replacement need to share the real CPU owner's revision and lifetime. This change adds the G1-a internal seam under the original IRQ-safe CPU owner lock, closes replaced/deleted owners irreversibly, preserves outstanding final charges, and keeps malformed writes and failed lifetime checks from advancing metadata. It includes 10 kernel tests against the actual owner.

Production bootstrap still does not bind a native resource. QueryAbi remains the only supported HOS2 operation. This PR does not enable native grants, successful resource effects, durable Hepta K/D, trusted-init, or desktop/mobile device control.

## Reproducible build and regression coverage

- Preserve the original upstream 234-package lock seed. Derive the working root lock only by adding the local os-control dependency and its existing spin edge; no external package record changes.
- Make component-macro's full metadata lookup use --locked, retaining its required complete graph.
- Keep the fixed 200-package aster-core, 97-package OSTD and 204-package ordinary-product derived locks explicit.
- Add a reviewed-head/tree candidate runner which builds and boots the ordinary non-ktest kernel, then uses that same ELF for the original process/exec QueryAbi checks and all four valid but unsupported operations.
- Emit each candidate marker and newline in one write, preserving strict exact-line acceptance and both historical A05 files byte for byte.
- Extend normal A06 CI with the candidate run and actual ELF retention. The existing complete kernel tests and one/two-vCPU quota/lifecycle probes remain required.

Developer documentation is in docs/ASTERINAS_CPU_OWNER_G1A.md, tests/kernel/control/README.md and the updated build manuals. The root README remains empty.

## Actual local validation

- aster-core: 179 passed, including all 10 new owner tests.
- OSTD: 221 reported passed, including 3 explicitly reported unsupported VMX/EPT soft skips; executed lower bound 218.
- Ordinary product and QueryAbi attempt 03: both raw QEMU exits 33; 14 exact markers each once; all 5,851 tracked paths matched the reviewed Git bytes/modes before and after. The generated ordinary lock matched the fixed 204-package lock.
- 16 host runner fixtures and strict static C compilation passed. Independent source, actual ELF/initramfs, serial, lock and snapshot review found no code blocker.
- The initial genuine Rust build failure, marker framing failure and later temporary-manifest collision are retained as failures in the R10 evidence package.

Kernel-test source was 12e0547d2e6394548b15764b06346422c4fff31e. Ordinary-product/probe source was 4e077aef4913179a68aa0d814018ce1a9d87cafc. Kernel, os-control and build inputs are byte-identical between those revisions. The initial published commit f744fb248a6d264676d0b892d21d6c4582d72d0f has exactly the tested ordinary-product tree 4e42c3833746cd2684d0a75020d73286820457e6. Git API publication changes commit identity, not its tree.

## Remaining observation and limits

The accepted third attempt ended with an empty Git status, but later workspace inspections again observed an untracked generated OSDK.toml. Its reappearance writer is unknown. This observation is retained separately, and the source gate and ignore rules were not weakened. The published tree contains only the reviewed Git objects; normal GitHub CI must independently exercise the strict gate.

This is G1-a. Complete CPU settlement/BOOTTIME/SMP accounting, production Process/exec grants, native operations and durable Hepta integration remain later gates.

## Normal CI follow-up

The original f744 A06 run 39193294713 / job 117870536573 passed. Its actual 18,333,821-byte artifact was independently reviewed: the three complete source snapshots match the exact Git tree, all 10 G1 kernel tests appear once, 14 QueryAbi markers appear once, and the original one/two-vCPU probes pass. This does not turn the original G0/A03 failures green.

G0 exposed a stale prefetch test API and a whole-workflow ELF string count that did not account for retained binary evidence. A03 first exposed an unregistered cfg(ktest) name in the independent Loom crate. Commit 463f70e36df6571faf6db45975d433ca10b0ddf6 (local bc778b6b8114e5017a467c0566f5777d85abafaf; tree 0218fa196b3ebb7a3f91c77906ab4ce30a67afe8) corrected those three host contracts. All 36 spec tests passed locally. The real preparation entry point still audits the immutable seed and derived packages; a negative fixture rejects changed locked-fetch input before metadata.

On 463f, normal G0 and A06 passed and both Loom variants passed, but the allocator fixture's separate generated manifest had the same missing cfg name and failed strict Clippy before any runtime scenario. The actual failure log and artifact are retained.

The host-corrected published head was 107afb7436ca17177262fdfef2e6b5dfee13597a, with exactly local bccb817e0d3f1987f59c1b9e7d94e939d2e6d1d3's tree 65ddb50cd303f3c43a8226141c5298dca369db5d. Its only additional change registers cfg(ktest) in that generated allocator manifest. Neither fixture enables the cfg; unsafe_code=forbid, warning severity and -D warnings remain intact. The kernel, os-control and product build inputs are unchanged.

Final local host verification passed: ABI 78 tests; os-control 225 tests under each of two backends (overlapping coverage, not 450 independent cases); strict Clippy/format and the no-std portable rlib; Loom 13 default models / 26,675 schedules and 6 public-backend models / 578 schedules; and 19 original allocator scenarios with zero allocation, reallocation or deallocation under internal locks. The final normal remote CI is still required before merge.

## Current-main integration

The six ordinary checks on 107afb7436ca17177262fdfef2e6b5dfee13597a all completed successfully, including G0, A03 and A06. Their original artifacts remain separately bound to that exact source.

Main then advanced through independently merged #196 to e15ae6a63edb5d4e7c475a001be82111d451b653, bringing Runtime freshness, process-boundary fixes and an A04 main-branch handoff manual. The current head 1c05412e2b340bbc8cd2b8a3389ae0ecce538991 merges that main without discarding its 567 changed paths. Its tree 2b873aa43445c8a02351f5900074a38c6fa4820d exactly matches local integration commit 1ca738c6310c50565804c2ea2a5d413a74bbe80a. Of the original 33 G1 changed paths, only docs/ASTERINAS_CPU_BANDWIDTH_N0.md needed a content merge; it retains both independent sections. All kernel, library, build, runner and test changes are byte-identical to the qualified 107afb candidate.

This head is now running the normal checks on the integrated source. Its source snapshots must reflect the actual new tree; the previous 5,851-file snapshots are not relabelled as this head's results.

Problem and change

Ordinary CPU configuration changes and controller replacement need to share the real CPU owner's revision and lifetime. This change adds the G1-a internal seam under the original IRQ-safe CPU owner lock, closes replaced/deleted owners irreversibly, preserves outstanding final charges, and keeps malformed writes and failed lifetime checks from advancing metadata. It includes 10 kernel tests against the actual owner.

Production bootstrap still does not bind a native resource. QueryAbi remains the only supported HOS2 operation. This PR does not enable native grants, successful resource effects, durable Hepta K/D, trusted-init, or desktop/mobile device control.

## Reproducible build and regression coverage

- Preserve the original upstream 234-package lock seed. Derive the working root lock only by adding the local os-control dependency and its existing spin edge; no external package record changes.
- Make component-macro's full metadata lookup use --locked, retaining its required complete graph.
- Keep the fixed 200-package aster-core, 97-package OSTD and 204-package ordinary-product derived locks explicit.
- Add a reviewed-head/tree candidate runner which builds and boots the ordinary non-ktest kernel, then uses that same ELF for the original process/exec QueryAbi checks and all four valid but unsupported operations.
- Emit each candidate marker and newline in one write, preserving strict exact-line acceptance and both historical A05 files byte for byte.
- Extend normal A06 CI with the candidate run and actual ELF retention. The existing complete kernel tests and one/two-vCPU quota/lifecycle probes remain required.

Developer documentation is in docs/ASTERINAS_CPU_OWNER_G1A.md, tests/kernel/control/README.md and the updated build manuals. The root README remains empty.

## Actual local validation

- aster-core: 179 passed, including all 10 new owner tests.
- OSTD: 221 reported passed, including 3 explicitly reported unsupported VMX/EPT soft skips; executed lower bound 218.
- Ordinary product and QueryAbi attempt 03: both raw QEMU exits 33; 14 exact markers each once; all 5,851 tracked paths matched the reviewed Git bytes/modes before and after. The generated ordinary lock matched the fixed 204-package lock.
- 16 host runner fixtures and strict static C compilation passed. Independent source, actual ELF/initramfs, serial, lock and snapshot review found no code blocker.
- The initial genuine Rust build failure, marker framing failure and later temporary-manifest collision are retained as failures in the R10 evidence package.

Kernel-test source was 12e0547d2e6394548b15764b06346422c4fff31e. Ordinary-product/probe source was 4e077aef4913179a68aa0d814018ce1a9d87cafc. Kernel, os-control and build inputs are byte-identical between those revisions. The initial published commit f744fb248a6d264676d0b892d21d6c4582d72d0f has exactly the tested ordinary-product tree 4e42c3833746cd2684d0a75020d73286820457e6. Git API publication changes commit identity, not its tree.

## Remaining observation and limits

The accepted third attempt ended with an empty Git status, but later workspace inspections again observed an untracked generated OSDK.toml. Its reappearance writer is unknown. This observation is retained separately, and the source gate and ignore rules were not weakened. The published tree contains only the reviewed Git objects; normal GitHub CI must independently exercise the strict gate.

This is G1-a. Complete CPU settlement/BOOTTIME/SMP accounting, production Process/exec grants, native operations and durable Hepta integration remain later gates.

## Normal CI follow-up

The original f744 A06 run 39193294713 / job 117870536573 passed. Its actual 18,333,821-byte artifact was independently reviewed: the three complete source snapshots match the exact Git tree, all 10 G1 kernel tests appear once, 14 QueryAbi markers appear once, and the original one/two-vCPU probes pass. This does not turn the original G0/A03 failures green.

G0 exposed a stale prefetch test API and a whole-workflow ELF string count that did not account for retained binary evidence. A03 first exposed an unregistered cfg(ktest) name in the independent Loom crate. Commit 463f70e36df6571faf6db45975d433ca10b0ddf6 (local bc778b6b8114e5017a467c0566f5777d85abafaf; tree 0218fa196b3ebb7a3f91c77906ab4ce30a67afe8) corrected those three host contracts. All 36 spec tests passed locally. The real preparation entry point still audits the immutable seed and derived packages; a negative fixture rejects changed locked-fetch input before metadata.

On 463f, normal G0 and A06 passed and both Loom variants passed, but the allocator fixture's separate generated manifest had the same missing cfg name and failed strict Clippy before any runtime scenario. The actual failure log and artifact are retained.

The host-corrected published head was 107afb7436ca17177262fdfef2e6b5dfee13597a, with exactly local bccb817e0d3f1987f59c1b9e7d94e939d2e6d1d3's tree 65ddb50cd303f3c43a8226141c5298dca369db5d. Its only additional change registers cfg(ktest) in that generated allocator manifest. Neither fixture enables the cfg; unsafe_code=forbid, warning severity and -D warnings remain intact. The kernel, os-control and product build inputs are unchanged.

Final local host verification passed: ABI 78 tests; os-control 225 tests under each of two backends (overlapping coverage, not 450 independent cases); strict Clippy/format and the no-std portable rlib; Loom 13 default models / 26,675 schedules and 6 public-backend models / 578 schedules; and 19 original allocator scenarios with zero allocation, reallocation or deallocation under internal locks. The final normal remote CI is still required before merge.

## Current-main integration

The six ordinary checks on 107afb7436ca17177262fdfef2e6b5dfee13597a all completed successfully, including G0, A03 and A06. Their original artifacts remain separately bound to that exact source.

Main then advanced through independently merged #196 to e15ae6a63edb5d4e7c475a001be82111d451b653, bringing Runtime freshness, process-boundary fixes and an A04 main-branch handoff manual. The current head 1c05412e2b340bbc8cd2b8a3389ae0ecce538991 merges that main without discarding its 567 changed paths. All kernel, library, build, runner and test changes are byte-identical to the qualified 107afb candidate.
